The derived fact “Erin is kind” contradicts the statement “Erin is not kind.” للم

2. Big, smart people are green. (If someone is big and smart, then green.)
3. If Erin is green then Erin is big. (If Erin green, then Erin big.)
4. If Erin is big then Erin is quiet. (If Erin big, then quiet.)
5. If someone is kind and big then they are furry. (If kind and big -> furry)
\Extension: "If someone is green then they are smart." (If green -> smart.)

We need to determine if Erin is kind. We have Erin green, Erin smart. We have rule 3: if Erin green then big. So Erin big. Rule 4: if Erin big then quiet. So Erin quiet. Now we have Erin smart and quiet. Rule 1: smart & quiet -> kind. So Erin kind. Therefore statement "Erin is not kind" is false. So answer: False.

- Rule 1: If someone is smart and quiet then kind. So derive: Erin kind.
- Therefore "Erin is not kind" contradicts derived kind. So statement is false.

But we should also consider rule "If someone is green then they are smart." Already given. But we have Erin green implies smart. Already fact. So no conflict.

Thus final answer: False.
